la:adj:seorsus.html:
sĕorsus, a, um, adj.
abbrev. from sevorsus, from se-vorto
,
sundered, separate, apart (syn. separatus).
Adj. (so only ante- and post-class.): seorsum atque diversum pretium, Cato ap. Fest. s. v. optionatus, p. 201 Müll.: vocabulum, id. ap. : syllabae, P.: seorsa quae (videor tractasse), ib.; cf. studia,.—Hence,
Adv.: sĕorsum (often erroneously written sĕorsim; collat. form sĕor-sus, ; Afran. ap. Charis, p. 195 P.; ; ; Cael. ap. Orell. N. cr.; Weissenb.; in both forms in the poets; usu. dissyl.; but trisyl. ; . —Another collat. form sorsum, ; ; ; ; cf. Lachm. ad ), asunder, separately, apart (syn. separatim; freq., but mostly ante-class.; not found in Cæs., Verg., or Hor.; and in Cic. only once, in the etymological definition of the word seditio).
With ab: me hodie senex seduxit solum, sorsum ab aedibus, Fleck.; so, seorsum ab rege exercitum ductare,: seorsum tractandum est hoc ab illo,: seorsum a collegā omnia paranda, Cael. ap. : abs te seorsum sentio,otherwise, differently,; cf.; ut abs te seorsus sentiam De uxoriā re, Afran. ap Charis, p. 195 P.—
With abl. (Lucretian): seorsum corpore,: animā, MSS. (Lachm. and Munro, animae).—
Absol.: quā arte natio sua separata seorsum, Cato ap. ; : in aediculam istanc seorsum concludi volo,; in custodiā habitus,; cf. : castris positis, Auct. B. Afr. 48, 2: ea dissensio civium, quod seorsum eunt alii ad alios, seditio dicitur,: omnibus gratiam habeo, et seorsum tibi praeterea, * : proin, viator, hunc deum vereberis, Manumque seorsum habebis,wilt hold afar,
